rec.name: Cart Drawer Sticky Elements & Scroll Settings (Sticky Checkout Button, Progress Bar, Payment Icons)
rec.status: Built — launched (reduced scope: only checkout button, progress bar and payment icons can be sticky)

what.text: Settings in the cart drawer (mini-cart) section that keep key cart elements pinned while the rest of the cart scrolls. The checkout button can be sticky at the top or bottom of the drawer. The free-shipping/reward progress bar can stick to the top. The payment icons and store benefits bar can stick to the bottom. The whole cart drawer scrolls when its content does not fit on one screen. The sticky checkout button uses the inverse of a PDP sticky ATC: a cloned button is shown only while the original in-flow button is out of view, and it hides as soon as the original becomes visible.

why.text: Cart drawers with upsells, recommendations and notes push the checkout CTA below the fold, so shoppers have to scroll to find the next step. A persistent checkout CTA keeps the primary action always visible and reduces friction and drop-off. A sticky progress bar keeps the free-shipping or reward goal in view, which strengthens goal-gradient motivation and AOV. Sticky payment icons and store benefits give constant trust reassurance at the moment of purchase decision.

how.text: Built as theme-level code in the cart drawer section, not a pure no-code block. 1) Add schema settings to mini-cart.liquid: enable_sticky_button (checkbox, default on), sticky_button_position (top/bottom, default bottom), enable_sticky_progressbar (checkbox, default off), enable_sticky_paymenticons (checkbox, default off). 2) Add a conditional <style> block: the progress bar uses CSS position: sticky at top: 0 with a white background and negative gutter margins. The drawer is made scrollable (overflow-y: auto) and the footer transform is removed. The checkout button and payment icons are cloned and use position: fixed, because they sit inside the cart footer and CSS sticky breaks once the parent scrolls out of view. Add top padding to the drawer when the button is sticky at the top. When both the button and payment icons are sticky at the bottom, offset the button by the payment-icon height via a CSS variable. 3) Add a JS scroll listener on #mini-cart that clones #checkout-button-wrapper and #payment-icons-and-store-benefits once, then shows or hides each clone depending on whether the original is in the viewport. 4) In theme.js, after the cart drawer innerHTML is re-rendered, call checkCheckoutButtonVisibility() after about 800ms so the sticky state is rebuilt after cart updates.

items: Enable sticky checkout button (checkbox, default on)
Sticky button position: Top / Bottom (default Bottom)
Enable sticky progress bar (checkbox, default off)
Enable sticky payment icons and store benefits (checkbox, default off)

dependencies.text: Needs edits to the theme's mini-cart.liquid section and theme.js (the re-render hook). Assumes element IDs and classes: #mini-cart, .drawer__footer, .shipping-bar, #checkout-button-wrapper, #payment-icons-and-store-benefits, and the CSS variable --container-gutter. Depends on the shipping/reward progress bar and the payment icons and store benefits element existing in the cart. No metafields. The original goal that every cart element be its own sticky-capable section was NOT delivered. The JS clone approach is fragile against later structural changes to the cart markup. Too many elements stuck to the same edge will overlap.
